'''Rachel Sarah Herz''' is a Canadian and American [[psychologist]] and [[Cognitive neuroscience|cognitive neuroscientist]], recognized for her research on the psychology of [[Olfaction|smell]].

== Background ==

Rachel Herz completed her undergraduate degree in psychology and biology at [[Queen's University at Kingston|Queen's University]] in [[Kingston, Ontario]], and an MA and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in the Psychology Department at the [[University of Toronto]]. After completing her PhD in 1992, she won a [[Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council]] (NSERC) Post-Doctoral Award and took her research to the [[University of British Columbia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aromamedical.com/articles/IATA.htm|title=IATA conference<!-- Bot generated title -->|website=aromamedical.com|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120721051422/http://www.aromamedical.com/articles/IATA.htm|archivedate=2012-07-21}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.rachelherz.com/home.html|title=Rachel Herz CV|last=|first=|date=|website=Rachel Herz|access-date=2019-12-03}}</ref> In 1994, she received the Ajinomoto USA Inaugural Award for Promising Young Scientists and joined the [[Monell Chemical Senses Center]] in Philadelphia as an assistant member.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bcft.ca/TECHTALK/january2005.pdf|title=insert.pmd<!-- Bot generated title -->|website=bcft.ca|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929081241/http://www.bcft.ca/TECHTALK/january2005.pdf|archivedate=2007-09-29}}</ref>

In 2000, Herz joined the faculty at [[Brown University]], first as a member of the Psychology Department and now as an adjunct assistant professor in the Department of Psychiatry and Human Behavior of Brown University Medical School.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Herz, Rachel|url=https://vivo.brown.edu/display/rherz|access-date=2020-10-21|website=vivo.brown.edu|language=en}}</ref> She was part-time faculty in the Department of Psychology and Neuroscience at Boston College from 2013-2022.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rachel Herz - Psychology Department - Morrissey College of Arts and Sciences - Boston College|url=https://www.bc.edu/bc-web/schools/mcas/departments/psychology/people/part-time-faculty/rachel-herz.html|access-date=2020-10-21|website=www.bc.edu}}</ref> Herz is a multiple TED-X speaker<ref>{{Cite web|first1=John |last1=Laidler |date=January 15, 2019 |title=TEDxNatick boasts an array of speakers - The Boston Globe|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/globelocal/2019/01/15/tedxnatick-boasts-array-speakers/ZGLkbZMzNZE69MDLIixiGK/story.html|access-date=2020-07-24|website=BostonGlobe.com|language=en-US}}</ref> and since the mid-1990s Herz has been consulting for many of the world's leading multinational fragrance and flavor companies and regularly lectures to national and international audiences.<ref>{{Cite web|title=This Friday: A public keynote lecture by Dr Rachel Herz in Wageningen! – NOSE|date=May 20, 2019 |url=http://www.nosenetwork.nl/this-friday-a-public-keynote-lecture-by-dr-rachel-herz-in-wageningen/|access-date=2020-07-24|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In 2004 Herz had to change her relationship with Brown University to a more limited involvement so that she could pursue other creative enterprises. It was at this time that she began writing ''The Scent of Desire: Discovering Our Enigmatic Sense of Smell'' ([[William Morrow and Company|William Morrow]]/[[Harper Collins Publishers]]) as well as working on other means to educate and stimulate the general public about the chemical senses. Her commercial ventures include The Educated Palate.<ref>{{cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Educated Palate Team|url=https://www.educatedpalate.com/about-us|access-date=|website=The Educated Palate}}</ref>

Herz has Canadian and American citizenship.<ref name=":0" /> Her father was the mathematician [[Carl S. Herz]].

== Psychology of smell ==
Her work examines with how language and emotion can affect odor perception and her laboratory has empirically demonstrated the first instance of olfactory illusions created by words alone.<ref>Herz, R.S. (2005). "The unique interaction between language and olfactory perception and cognition", ''Trends in Experimental Psychology Research'', (pp. 91-109). New York: [[Nova Science Publishers, Inc.]]</ref><ref>Herz, R.S. (2003). "The effect of verbal context in olfactory perception", ''Journal of Experimental Psychology: General'', 132, 595-606.</ref> Herz also studies how we perceive food and how food-based emotions influence us. Theoretically guided by perspectives from [[cognitive psychology]] and [[evolutionary biology]], Herz uses [[Psychophysics|psychophysical]], self-report, cognitive-behavioral and neurological techniques, including [[functional magnetic resonance imaging]] (fMRI), to investigate these topics.

== Outreach ==

Herz serves on several advisory boards, including the UK charity for smell loss, Fifth Sense.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Advisory Board – Fifth Sense|url=https://www.fifthsense.org.uk/whoweare/the-advisory-board/|access-date=2020-10-21|language=en-GB}}</ref> Herz serves on several advisory boards and councils, including the Smell and Taste Association of North America, the UK charity for smell loss, Fifth Sense, the Association for Chemoreception Sciences<ref>{{Cite web |title=Association for Chemoreception Sciences |url=https://achems.org/web/about-committees.php |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=achems.org}}</ref> and OVRTechnology<ref>{{Cite web |title=About {{!}} Enhance Digital Experiences Today |url=https://www.ovrtechnology.com/about |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=OVR TECHNOLOGY |language=en-US}}</ref> Her research on sensory memory was on display from 2001 to 2006 in a traveling [[Smithsonian Institution]] exhibit called "Brain: The world inside your head".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pfizer.com/brain/|title=Our Purpose - Pfizer: One of the world's premier biopharmaceutical companies|website=www.pfizer.com}}</ref> She has given numerous interviews, including for: [[CBC.ca|CBC]], ''The Science of the Senses'', @Discovery.ca (The Discovery Channel, Canada), The [[Discovery Channel]] USA, ABC Discovery News, ABC News, The BBC, National Geographic, [[NBC Nightly News|NBC Nightly news]], Korean Public Broadcasting, ABC ''The Chronicle'', FOX News, [[National Public Radio]], CBS ''The Early Show''. She is also featured in [[Mystify: Michael Hutchence]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mystify: Michael Hutchence|url=https://www.bbfc.co.uk/releases/mystify-michael-hutchence-video|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191203050436/https://bbfc.co.uk/releases/mystify-michael-hutchence-video|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 3, 2019|access-date=2020-10-21|website=www.bbfc.co.uk}}</ref>
